justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish baseline for the asset across all three horizons, with prices drifting gradually higher from roughly 309.5 at one day out to 314 at one month. The one-day estimate is anchored primarily by recent price momentum and the assumption that no major macro catalyst or overnight shock disrupts the prevailing trend. At the one-week horizon, I incorporated a slight upward drift consistent with a mild risk-on environment, while acknowledging that weekly price action tends to revert toward short-term moving averages in the absence of strong directional catalysts. The one-month estimate extends that gentle drift further, reflecting a baseline assumption that fundamental conditions remain broadly supportive without any significant deterioration in the macro backdrop.

The confidence interval widths widen considerably as the horizon extends, which reflects the compounding uncertainty inherent in longer forecast windows. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 13 points, capturing typical intraday-to-next-day volatility under normal market conditions. By one week, the interval expands to about 26 points, incorporating the possibility of a meaningful data release, central bank communication, or geopolitical development shifting sentiment. At one month, the interval widens to roughly 52 points, reflecting the reality that a month is long enough for entire narratives to shift — earnings surprises, inflation prints, or liquidity conditions can all materially reprice assets over that window.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals entirely. On the downside, an unexpected deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a sharp miss on employment or a surprise inflation spike — could trigger a flight to safety or forced de-risking that drives prices well below the lower bounds. A sudden tightening in financial conditions, whether from central bank hawkishness or a credit event, would pose similar risks. On the upside, a strong risk appetite surge driven by better-than-expected growth data, a geopolitical resolution, or a significant policy pivot could easily carry prices above the upper bounds of even the one-month interval.

It is also worth noting that these intervals assume relatively normal market functioning and liquidity. In periods of stress, bid-ask spreads widen, correlations shift, and tail events cluster in ways that standard volatility-based interval construction does not fully capture. Black swan events — a sudden geopolitical escalation, a major institutional failure, or an unexpected regulatory shock — could produce outcomes far outside any reasonable confidence interval constructed under normal distributional assumptions.
